independence: Fresh source and evidence review; no browser, build, product source edit, or native rerun in this lane.

evidence: The failed 0.2.215 run reached warm_media_controls and reported warm_image_size_groups_missing. Its receipt records three successfully loaded image sizes, 640x480, 96x96, and 32x32, but no Images-pane toolbar observation or failure screenshot.

ScrapeView authors the image toolbar with lowercase counts and applies uppercase CSS. The old driver compared lowercase text to content.innerText, making an observation error plausible. This is an inference, not a demonstrated cause of the failed run.

The repair reads textContent from the active Images-pane toolbar and exact img.src URLs from the three rendered grid classes. It asserts large/intake.svg, medium/appointment-card.svg, and icon/clinic-icon.svg initially and the exact surviving URLs after each of three selective removals.

The driver continues to use owned-page capture and observed DOM; this diff adds no production state injection. Existing media add/remove, video, tab, reload, screenshot, exact-artifact, and resource-health paths remain present.

The helper rejects wrong pane, hidden pane, swapped group URLs, stale membership after a removal, and an incorrect authored toolbar count. The existing assertMediaPane still checks exact visible links, loaded image dimensions, tab counts, and the absence of opposite-media rows.

Focused independent run: node --test tests/browser/scrape-media-assertions.test.mjs passed 7/7; pnpm compile passed. These synthetic helper checks do not prove that the native DOM selector sees the real pane.

Warm and reload media work are wrapped only to collect failure observations; the original error is rethrown and the outer catch retains its stage and failure code. The observation includes selected/visible state, at most 1200 characters of pane text, fixture-local media URLs, and a 0600 screenshot path or explicit capture errors. It is bounded for this controlled fixture, not a general-purpose redactor.

The three grid selectors depend on current UI class names, so a native run is required to validate that source reasoning against the browser. The failed run did not establish whether the grid classification itself was correct.

decision: NOMINATE exactly one guarded native rerun of the repaired exact artifact. A pass must include actual initial and post-removal group observations in warm and reload phases plus the existing resource and media gates; a failure must retain the original code and the new pane observation/screenshot. Do not call the feature passed before that run.
